what_is_not_known: The IRS yearly average for China for 2025 is 7.129. The Federal Reserve's annual average for 2025 is 7.1875, and its twelve monthly averages give the same figure. The gap is 0.0585, about 0.8%; for 2021 to 2024 the two sources differ by 0.007 or less. On $400,000 the choice moves the illustrated gain for 2025 money by $3,055. This page uses the Federal Reserve series throughout and shows the IRS figures beside it. Neither is called wrong here.
how_to_settle_it: Use the actual dates and one daily rate source for a real return. Ask the IRS how its 2025 figure was computed if it matters.

item: Which box this money is in
what_is_not_known: The statute and the regulation give the test (would the costs of the transaction be business or income-producing expenses) and two examples, a bond purchase and a holiday. They do not say where a savings balance, pay left in an account, or sale proceeds waiting to be sent home belong. The regulation's own bank-account example opens with 'Assume expenses associated with the demand account are deductible under section 212'. The box changes the rate and whether a loss counts.
how_to_settle_it: Write down what each part of the balance was for and take it to a U.S. tax professional. Both columns are shown on this page so the range is visible meanwhile.

item: Gift from someone who is not a U.S. taxpayer
what_is_not_known: A gift keeps the giver's basis. The texts read do not say how the dollar basis of RMB is measured when the giver never had to keep dollar records.
how_to_settle_it: Collect the giver's own dates of acquisition; a U.S. tax professional decides the method.

item: RMB acquired before the holder was a U.S. taxpayer
what_is_not_known: No rule for this case was found in the texts read, so the dollar cost for it is left blank in the table.
how_to_settle_it: A U.S. tax professional, with the dates.

item: Where an ordinary section 988 gain or loss goes on the return
what_is_not_known: No official page read in this pass names the line. Only non-official sites were found saying Schedule 1, and they are not relied on. How an ordinary loss is taken on an individual's return was not verified either.
how_to_settle_it: The preparer of the return; the Instructions for Form 1040 for the year.

item: Whether the 3.8% tax reaches a currency gain
what_is_not_known: The statute counts 'net gain … attributable to the disposition of property'. The regulation that defines net investment income does not mention foreign currency or section 988 (a full-text search of the current section returned nothing for either phrase). The ladder therefore shows the 3.8% in its own column, to be added only if it applies.
how_to_settle_it: A U.S. tax professional; the Instructions for Form 8960.

what_is_not_known: A transfer between deposits 'denominated in the same nonfunctional currency' is not taxed. Whether a mainland RMB deposit and an RMB deposit held outside the mainland are the same currency for this rule is not addressed in the text read.
how_to_settle_it: A U.S. tax professional, before moving RMB to an account outside the mainland.

item: Many small personal conversions and the $200 line
what_is_not_known: The $200 line is written per transaction. No official text read says how a run of small conversions of the same money is treated. This page does not suggest relying on it.

item: Averages stand in for real dates
what_is_not_known: The ladder prices the RMB at a yearly or monthly average because no acquisition dates have been supplied. A real figure uses the rate on each actual day.

item: Editions and dates of the texts
what_is_not_known: The U.S. Code was read in the 2024 edition on govinfo; changes enacted after that edition were not searched for. The 2026 figures are from Rev. The regulations were read on the eCFR, which says it is authoritative but unofficial.
how_to_settle_it: Re-read the linked pages before filing.
